title: Filmation castle templates
description: A Filmation castle's templates: the castle-wide pieces every room naming one is built from. rooms.json places them by name; rooms_source.py turns the two into room_data.s, and the templates editor opens this file. A template is keyed by its name and IS its list of placements. Its POSITION in its table is the game's own number for it -- Knight Lore's code takes scenery 0-7 to be the arches, and gives object templates behaviour by label -- so a template may be renamed but not moved, and a new one goes on the end.

meta.description: About the file. The game matters unless the file says otherwise: Knight Lore and Pentagram decide which templates are doorways by their position in the game's own table, and put them in different places. A castle that lists its own doorways and background here is taken at its word instead.

doorways.description: Which scenery templates are doorways, by name, and the wall each stands in. When this is here it is the whole list -- any template may be a doorway and no other is one -- and the builder reads a table made from it; without it the game's own rule by index applies. A rename in the designer carries the name across.

background.description: The scenery templates drawn first and never sorted, by exact name. When this is here it is the whole list; without it the game's own names apply.

rooms.description: The rooms file these templates belong to, beside this one. Required: nothing is assumed, and that file has to name this one back in its meta.templates.

sceneryTemplates.description: Walls, arches and trees: pieces placed at fixed world coordinates rather than on the floor grid. background_insert puts them in an unsorted run at the front of the draw list, so nothing is ever drawn behind them. Keyed by the name rooms call it by; a template IS its list of placements, in the order they are put down. The key ORDER is the game's table order, so a template may be renamed but not moved. The same graphic may be placed more than once -- a wall is one stone laid five times.

u.description: World U, towards the viewer; the floor is centred on 128. Scenery only -- an object takes its place from the room.

v.description: World V, away from the viewer.

sizeU.description: An override of the box graphics.json gives this graphic, for a record whose bytes are not a box at all -- Knight Lore's guard templates end with a blank, passable entry whose U and V are the guard's patrol extent. Give all three or none. Nothing else needs them: the box belongs to the graphic, and a mirrored piece swaps U and V by itself.

sizeV.description: Half-width along V, with sizeU and sizeZ.

offsets.description: Where inside its cell the piece sits. A cell is 16 units across, so a half offset is 8. Objects only.

raiseZ.description: Extra height above the floor, on top of the room's floorZ and the position's own z. Masked to a multiple of 4 by room_unpack.

objectTemplates.description: A group of objects placed together on the floor grid. A room names the template and then lists where to stamp it. Keyed by the name rooms call it by; a template IS its list of placements, in the order they are put down. The key ORDER is the game's table order, so a template may be renamed but not moved. The same graphic may be placed more than once -- a wall is one stone laid five times.

v.description: World V, away from the viewer.

graphic.description: A sprite's name from the sheet, not a number: a path through the sprite groups, then which one it is within its group, counting from one -- knight.legs.1. A frame shared by several graphic numbers takes the number as a last segment (knight.legs.1.g144), because they are not interchangeable. A graphic with no artwork at all is gfx_NN. graphics.py is the one place names and numbers meet; rooms_source.py stops on a name it cannot place rather than emit a wrong byte.

flags.description: The game's own flag byte. Two bits are known and named; the rest are carried whole rather than guessed at.

mirrored.description: Bit 6: draw the artwork the other way round. The nudge may differ when it is -- see graphic_map.json.

passable.description: Bit 1: things walk through it rather than into it.

rest.description: The bits we have not named, kept so the file claims no more than is actually known.
